title: DOJ nominee faces confirmation hurdle over agency commitments
summary: Todd Blanche’s confirmation faces a potential delay as senators seek written guarantees limiting Trump’s anti-weaponization fund and the scope of audit protections included in a Justice Department settlement agreement.

title: Staffing cuts are leaving federal statistical agencies stretched thin
summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics and Census Bureau have been hard hit by staffing cuts, and experts say replacing lost expertise won't happen overnight.

title: Inspectors general are conducting fewer oversight reports after 18 months of upheaval
summary: In a new report, the Partnership for Public Service noted that the average Cabinet inspector general office has shrunk by 19% since the end of 2024.

title: How TSA passenger screening became an immigration enforcement tool
summary: Newly released records reveal a formal agreement between TSA and ICE that expands how passenger data can be used, raising new questions about privacy, government data sharing and the agency's testimony to Congress.

title: Senate confirms Clayton as Trump’s next intelligence director
summary: The former SEC chairman will replace acting intelligence chief Bill Pulte, whose brief tenure oversaw repeated personnel cuts to the nation’s top spy office.

title: IRS and Social Security bar employees from taking advanced leave
summary: A union official says advanced leave functions as a sort of short-term or long-term disability insurance program for many federal employees.

title: New documentary recounts ‘free-for-all attitude of cruelty’ toward axed federal employees
summary: The movie, which was filmed during the start of the second Trump administration, examines the human and societal effects of recent federal job cuts.

title: Pulte announces 30% ODNI staff reduction hours before Clayton vote
summary: The acting intelligence chief said a fifth and “near final” round of terminations was underway Tuesday but did not disclose how many employees were affected.

title: AFGE sues over EEOC’s apparent shutdown of class action cases against agencies
summary: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Chairwoman Andrea Lucas surreptitiously ordered a halt on all class-action proceedings in which a federal agency is a defendant last December, despite regulations requiring such cases be handled “promptly.”

title: As presidents gain power, who keeps government accountable?
summary: COMMENTARY | The Supreme Court's decision expanding presidential authority over independent agencies is about more than executive power, it also raises the stakes for congressional oversight, agency leadership and the federal workforce.

title: Dem senators demand answers on SSA field office closures despite Bisignano’s vow
summary: Just weeks after the Social Security commissioner falsely accused his predecessor of turning away members of the public, lawmakers say Bisignano has done just that.

title: AI's growing role in rulemaking raises new transparency questions
summary: As the Trump administration pursues an aggressive deregulatory agenda, concerns are mounting that artificial intelligence could make agency decisions harder to explain and defend.

title: Government service delivery needs standard definitions, former government tech leaders say
summary: A new proposal urges Congress to align common definitions across federal programs, arguing the current patchwork creates administrative burdens and complicates service delivery.

title: As USDA relocation deadlines near, employees say questions remain unanswered
summary: Employees say they still lack key details about exemptions, moving costs and next steps as USDA continues issuing relocation notices.

title: Suit alleges DHS targeted people observing and protesting immigration agents
summary: Plaintiffs allege the department used technology to identify immigration observers before retaliating against them, including by revoking TSA PreCheck and Global Entry benefits.

title: Federal employees say they’ll quit if they have to move to New Jersey
summary: A bipartisan group of lawmakers is urging the Trump administration to reconsider the planned move of local offices of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

title: Bill aims to end blocked congressional access at federal buildings
summary: A new bill would set governmentwide rules for congressional visits after disputes over access to agencies and immigration detention centers.

title: NARFE still has concerns with OPM’s plan to collect employee health care records
summary: Last month, the Office of Personnel Management sought to assuage concerns about its request for claims-level data on federal workers’ health insurance usage. Employee groups say it’s still not enough.

title: Attorney general nomination faces another week of scrutiny
summary: The postponed Judiciary Committee vote gives senators more time to scrutinize Todd Blanche's record and leaves questions about key Republican support unresolved.

title: Selective Service System seeks software to aid the draft
summary: If the military draft were to ever come back, this software would be used to quickly evaluate staffing and resource requirements.
